BLOCKING BUG found in personas/standalone/src/content/pipeline-configurator.md: the 'documentation-only chain' is defined as ["documentation", "qa", "code-review"], which violates the mcp-server canonical stage ordering constraint. The MCP server enforces that active_pipeline_stages must be a subsequence of [implementation, qa, security-audit, code-review, release-engineering, documentation]. This invalid chain would cause a hard error on ledger_create_work_package for all documentation-only WPs.
Non-blocking: the pre-existing lack of mcpServers support in standalone CC frontmatter is a known limitation, appropriately flagged by Developer and QA.

comments.note: BLOCKING: personas/standalone/src/content/pipeline-configurator.md defines the documentation-only chain as ["documentation", "qa", "code-review"]. This ordering violates the canonical stage constraint enforced in mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (lines 367-381): stages must be a strict subsequence of CANONICAL_PIPELINE_ORDERING = [implementation, qa, security-audit, code-review, release-engineering, documentation]. Passing 'documentation' at position 0 followed by 'qa' will exhaust the canonical scan and throw: 'Pipeline stages are out of canonical order.' Any documentation-only WP would fail ledger_create_work_package. The same invalid chain appears in the Output Format example table (WP-003 row). Fix: replace both occurrences with ['documentation'] (solo stage) or ['qa', 'code-review', 'documentation'] (with validation — though semantically inverted, it is technically valid). The solo ['documentation'] chain is simplest since doc-only WPs have no code to QA or review.

BLOCKING BUG in personas/standalone/src/content/ledger-bootstrapper.md Step 3 protocol: the instruction lists 'work_package_id: e.g., WP-001' as a parameter to pass to ledger_create_work_package, but that parameter does not exist in the tool schema — WP IDs are auto-generated. This violates AC-2 ('clear input/output contracts') since it teaches agents incorrect API usage. Zod's strip mode prevents a hard failure in the common case, but: (a) the agent is given a false belief that it controls the WP ID; (b) there is no guidance to capture the auto-generated ID from the response for use in dependency references of subsequent WPs.

comments.note: Gold Nugget: the 4-role decomposition of PM work (decomposer → sequencer → configurator → bootstrapper) is a clean, well-separated responsibility model. Each agent has a narrow, non-overlapping concern and can be invoked independently. This pattern is reusable for future PM expansion.

BLOCKING: personas/standalone/src/content/ledger-bootstrapper.md Step 3 lists 'work_package_id: e.g., WP-001' as a parameter to pass to ledger_create_work_package, but this parameter does not exist in the tool schema (see api-surface.md line 130–155 and system tool definition). WP IDs are auto-generated. Zod strips unknown params silently, so it won't cause a hard runtime error for fresh sequential projects. However: (1) the protocol teaches agents incorrect API usage — a false belief that they can control the WP ID; (2) the protocol does not tell the agent to capture the auto-generated ID from the response and use that captured value when specifying dependencies for subsequent WPs. If a ledger is not fresh (prior WPs exist), the auto-generated IDs will not be WP-001, WP-002 etc. and dependency references will be wrong. Fix: remove work_package_id from the parameter list; add a note that the WP ID is auto-generated and returned in the tool response; instruct the agent to capture that returned ID and use it in dependency arrays for subsequent create calls.

Non-blocking: the bootstrapper protocol in Step 3 says 'in dependency order' but does not clarify what to do if the auto-generated sequential IDs diverge from the IDs used in the dependency arrays of the WP spec files. A brief note explaining that for fresh ledgers IDs are assigned sequentially starting from WP-001 would reduce agent confusion.
